Read docs/TASK_MEGATRON_V3.md FIRST (in your context): section 2.1 gives every input shape, section 3 lists the examples your test must prove. Every name you need is there or below; do not invent names, keys, numbers or files. Python 3.9-compatible syntax (typing.List/Dict/Optional; no `match`, no `X | Y`), standard library only. Tests are unittest, `maxDiff = None` in every TestCase, `msg=` on every assertion, one test method per numbered example, each test's docstring names the example (e.g. `U example 1`). Fixtures are loaded from `os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "fixtures")`; never modify them. No test opens a network connection: no urlopen, no sockets.

Write ONLY your one test file. Do not write or modify anything under megatron/ or any existing test -- the code is already shipped; you are the author of the criterion, not of the code. Import the code under test through its module and call it at call time, so a mutated copy of the module is what runs. 

## Store upsert must UPDATE the row (U.1)

Why: the only upsert test saves the SAME record twice and counts rows, so a save_experts that silently ignores the second insert passes all 56 tests. Your test must make the update observable.

Write `tests/test_store_upsert.py` proving spec section 3 example U.1. Record A is the dict given verbatim in spec section 2.1 (write it as a module-level literal); Record B is a copy of A with exactly followers 325474, total_stars 262428, expertise_score 850330. In a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory db: `storage.save_experts(db, [A])` returns 1, `storage.save_experts(db, [B])` returns 1, `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM experts` via sqlite3 is 1 (close the connection), and `storage.top_experts(db, 10) == [B]` (whole list of whole dicts). Use `from megatron import storage`. The acceptance runs your test against two mutants of storage.py (INSERT OR IGNORE; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and requires it to FAIL on both.

Why: the only error test uses 404, so a client that raises only for status > 400 passes all 56 tests. Your test must sit on the boundary.

Write `tests/test_client_status_boundary.py` proving spec section 3 example S.1. The acceptance runs your test against a github_client.py mutated to `if status > 400:` and requires it to FAIL.

## Concurrency limit is observable (K.1, K.2)

Why: no fake fetcher counts calls in flight, so a collect_profiles with its semaphore removed passes all 56 tests. Your test must observe the peak.

Write `tests/test_collect_concurrency.py` proving spec section 3 examples K.1 and K.2. logins = ["karpathy", "openai", "google", "huggingface", "rafaballerini"]. Build a fresh fake per run, with a state dict {in_flight, peak, calls}: `async def fetch_json(path)` increments in_flight and calls, sets peak = max(peak, in_flight), then in try/finally awaits `asyncio.sleep(0.01)` and returns a deep copy of parsed tests/fixtures/repos_torvalds.json when path ends with `/repos?per_page=100`, else of parsed tests/fixtures/user_torvalds.json; finally decrements in_flight. K.1: `asyncio.run(collectors.collect_profiles(logins, fetch_json, concurrency=2))` -> peak == 2, calls == 10, 5 results, none is None. K.2: concurrency=1 -> peak == 1, 5 results, none is None. Use `from megatron import collectors` and call `collectors.collect_profiles` at call time. The acceptance runs your test against two mutants of collectors.py (semaphore removed; Semaphore(concurrency + 1)) and requires it to FAIL on both.
